findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a concrete proving step for AC5: either a fixture-based test asserting the compiled prompt contains the three named false-positive guards, or an explicit rationale that the guard behavior is validated at Pass-2/Pass-3 review time rather than by an in-session command.
evidence: AC5: 'The reviewer prompt carries the false-positive guards ... so a compliant lockstep change or a justified divergence returns no finding.'
Testing enumerates: OVERLAY_IDS membership, routing_index shape, threshold_for, glob firing/inert, index.json byte-identity drift — none exercises the prompt's guard behavior on a diff.
ABSENCE: no described step maps to AC5's 'returns no finding' behavioral outcome; it is verifiable in-session only as prompt-text presence, not as reviewer behavior.
findings.finding: AC5 makes a behavioral claim ('a compliant lockstep change or a justified divergence returns no finding') but the Testing section proves only registration/routing/drift, not that the reviewer prompt's false-positive guards actually suppress a finding on a compliant/justified diff.
scenarios: A future prompt edit weakens a false-positive guard and no test catches it because AC5 has no proving step.
AC5 is checked off on the basis of prompt text existing, while the guard clause is malformed or missing.
findings.suggested_fix: State in Testing that AC5 is proven by asserting the packaged prompt's front-matter/body contains the enumerated false-positive guard clauses (deliberate justified divergence; adapter-bound non-caller-visible params; internal-only refactor), since the agentic reviewer's runtime behavior is non-deterministic and intentionally advisory.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how AC5's guarantee is validated: add a prompt-behavior fixture/eval exercising (a) a genuine one-sided surface divergence -> finding and (b) a justified-divergence / adapter-bound-param / internal-refactor case -> no finding, or explicitly defer that behavioral validation to a named ticket.
evidence: Testing lists only: OVERLAY_IDS membership, routing_index shape, threshold_for, glob FIRES/inert, index.json drift, lint/typecheck.
AC5: 'The reviewer prompt carries the false-positive guards ... so a compliant lockstep change or a justified divergence returns no finding.'

The prompt behavior (fire on genuine one-sided divergence; stay silent on justified divergence / adapter-bound params / internal refactor) is the substantive deliverable but is only asserted, not validated by any test named in the plan.
findings.finding: The plan's core deliverable is the reviewer prompt and its false-positive guards, yet the Testing section only verifies the mechanical wiring (OVERLAY_IDS membership, routing shape, threshold_for, glob fire/inert, index.json drift) — it never exercises the prompt's actual finding/no-finding JUDGMENT. Acceptance Criterion 5 ('a compliant lockstep change or a justified divergence returns no finding') and the stated true-positive behavior (flags a one-sided param/guard change) have no corresponding test or named validation path, so the whole point of the overlay could be non-functional while the suite goes green.
scenarios: A regression that neuters the false-positive guards ships green because no test covers the justified-divergence no-finding path.
A prompt edit that stops firing on a genuine one-sided surface change (the escaped-bug class this ticket targets) is not caught because no true-positive-divergence fixture exists.

findings.checklist_item: State the overlay's scope boundary vs the recorded shape-inspection blind spot — explicitly that it coaches DECLARED-surface (param/guard/required-field) lockstep and defers RUNTIME conditional-required parity to the topaz behavioral oracle — so it is not mistaken for a behavioral-parity guarantee.
evidence: restoring-shallow-blobfish experiment comment: 'the earlier naive signature-parity experiment ... fired on 4/5 ops with FALSE-POSITIVES (force_close/source/return_alias/_creation_channel) and was BLIND to the runtime close_class rule.'

Same ticket deep-dive (G4): 'THE REAL PARITY RISK IS BEHAVIORAL, and generation [/shape inspection] cannot express it ... close_class defaults to "" on EVERY surface, but "required" is a RUNTIME rule ... A generated surface would look identical yet still diverge on exactly what this ticket cares about -> false confidence.'

The plan carries FP guards for the named adapter-bound params (adapter-bound `_creation_channel`/`return_alias`/`source`/`repo_root`), which addresses the recorded false-positive set, but it does not acknowledge or bound the recorded shape-inspection BLIND SPOT to the runtime rule.
findings.finding: The plan's static Grep-the-siblings approach does not engage this ticket's own recorded finding that a naive signature/shape-parity check produces false-positives and is BLIND to the runtime conditional-required rules (G4) that are the true parity hazard — the exact reason the finalized design chose the behavioral oracle (topaz), not a shape check.
findings.location: Approach section (step 1: 'tells the reviewer to Grep the sibling adapters for the changed param/guard')
scenarios: A diff keeps the `close_class` param present on all three adapters (parity looks fine to a static reviewer) but changes the runtime 'required iff bug-close' rule on only one path — the surface-parity overlay, judging param/guard presence, would see parity and stay silent, reproducing the G4 blind spot the oracle was built to catch.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to the Approach/Portability framing scoping surface-parity to caller-visible surface lockstep and citing the topaz oracle as the authority for runtime behavioral parity (G4), acknowledging the recorded signature-parity experiment.

findings.checklist_item: Justify surface-parity as distinct from api-compat's existing 'asymmetric interface change' detection (e.g. write-adapter-specific triggering, required-field/guard scope api-compat does not cover, or advisory-vs-blocking posture), or fold it into api-compat.
evidence: code-review-api-compat.md lines 26-29: 'asymmetric interface change: one side of an interface contract is updated but not its counterpart — a function signature changes (added/renamed/reordered/removed parameter, changed return shape) but Grep shows callsites still using the old form.'

The plan proposes surface-parity to flag 'when a write-op's parameter / guard / required-field surface changes on ONE adapter ... without the sibling surfaces being updated in lockstep' — an adapter-to-sibling asymmetric-interface case api-compat already covers.

ANTI-REPACKAGING/Rule-of-Three: the plan models ON api-compat but never states why api-compat's asymmetric-interface detection is insufficient for the write-adapter case, so it risks repackaging an existing overlay under a new id.
findings.finding: The plan does not distinguish the proposed surface-parity overlay from the EXISTING api-compat overlay, which already detects 'asymmetric interface change' (a signature param added/renamed/removed on one side while Grep shows the counterpart still using the old form) — substantially the same defect class the surface-parity overlay targets.
findings.location: Approach section ('Model it on the existing GLOB-triggered overlays (api-compat, security)')
scenarios: A diff adds a `reason` param to `_lib_writes.py` but not `_mcp_writes.py`: both api-compat (asymmetric interface) and the new surface-parity overlay would fire, producing duplicate/overlapping findings on the same change.
